- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) due to momentum bias; apply downward correction of 1–3% for final 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is high and price is flat or slightly declining, model tends to overreact; apply a “sentiment dampening” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day if sentiment >0.75 and price < prior 3-day average.
